Q1: In failed review run `37800211275` (or any later failed run on `drhyg_ecommerce_automation#64`, head `c7729abf`), which step failed and what error did it print?
Choices:
A. "Install project dependencies (best-effort)" failed: `review_untrusted_sandbox.sh prepare` printed `::error::Review dependency isolation failed`. That covers the 900s `timeout` at line 93, an OOM kill under `--memory 3g`, or `python3 -m venv` failing at line 111. Please name which one.
B. "Apply fixes with editor model" failed or exited without writing a summary. Please give the first error line from the `previous_reviews/editor_attempt_*.err` artifact.
C. The logs and artifacts can't be retrieved, so the failing step is unknown. Use Q2 to set the scope. (RECOMMENDED)
**Note:** Q2 only applies if you choose Q1:C. With Q1:A or Q1:B, the fix targets the confirmed step and Q2 is ignored.
Q2: If the root cause can't be confirmed (Q1:C), what should this heal change do?
Choices:
A. Make the failure diagnosable without changing how anything runs. When the editor phase ends as `editor_empty_noop`, put the tail of the dependency-prep log or the editor attempt stderr into the failure evidence and the failure comment. Name the step that failed. Stop reporting a synthetic `attempt_count` of 1 when no `editor_attempt_*` artifact exists; the field stays, only its value becomes accurate. Add regression tests for these. The root-cause fix is left to the next lineage generation, which will then have the evidence. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Act on the unconfirmed dependency-timeout theory: treat a dependency-container `timeout` exit (124) as a best-effort install failure (warning only), while isolation, snapshot and refresh failures stay fatal. **Note:** this is unconfirmed and may not remove the actual cause.
C. Make no code change. Escalate this issue to a human until the run logs are supplied.
